speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To understand your wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions, I need to know if you have any recent joint swelling, redness, or morning stiffness. Have you had any recent insect bites, travel, or new animal exposures?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of recent camping in Minnesota combined with left knee pain followed by wrist involvement and fever is highly concerning for Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. Did you notice a bull's-eye rash or any other specific rash patterns during your illness? Also, have you noticed any discharge from the urethra or pain in your testicles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.
